newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier sets CRJ-700 program cost.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier sets CRJ-700 program cost.

text.p: Bombardier Inc said on Wednesday the program cost for the development of its new 70-seat Canadair Regional Jet Series 700 is C$645 million.

Robert Brown, president of Bombardier Aerospace told a news conference Bombardier will be responsible for C$440 million of the program cost, while the rest will be shared by the project's various suppliers.
He said the cost figures do not include the new aircraft's power plant and engines, which are being developed by General Electric Co.

Pierre Lortie, president of Bombardier Regional Aircraft Division, said the company has four firm orders for the CRJ-700 from Brit Air of France, and 28 options and 35 memoranda of understanding from a total of eight airlines. He declined to name the other airlines.
Lortie said the CRJ-700 will have a sale price of US$23 million, in 1995 dollars.
Brown also said Bombardier continues to have talks with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd regarding the possible development of a 100-seat jet.
"Yes, we are having some discussions with Mitsubishi," Brown told reporters.
But he added that unlike the CRJ-700, Bombardier would not likely take a lead role in any development or manufacture of a 100-seat jet, "but anything is possible."
Mitsubishi is one of the international suppliers who are partners in the manufacture of the CRJ-700.
Mitsubishi is expected to obtain final approval from its board to manufacture the aft section of the fuselage for the CRJ-700.
